data.body:
RESOLVED via Gerrit change 1622 (merged as abc3afd7db on gerrit/main; LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, CI run 31561539010 success).

Chosen trigger word: `rerun-llm-review`. It shares no substring in either direction with any `[mapping "comment-added"]` key in infra/gerrit/gerrit_to_platform.ini.template (the only key is `recheck`). The CI-side mapping was deliberately left untouched — that word is theirs.

Hard cutover, no alias window. The retired word now queues nothing, writes no label, and draws a single refusal reply naming the new trigger. The refusal is placed after the project guard and after the change re-anchoring, since post_comment needs the re-anchored change_id/revision and the bot must never reply off-project.

SECOND BUG FOUND AND FIXED (not in the original scope): the bot's own reply texts — _ACCEPTED_MESSAGE and _refusal_message — embedded the retired word verbatim. Those are posted as Gerrit comments, so every reply the bot sent was itself re-dispatching the Verified workflow. All reply texts are now scrubbed, and the retired-word refusal describes the old word rather than spelling it.

Two tests parse the ini template at test time rather than hardcoding `recheck`: one asserts substring-disjointness in both directions, the other asserts no bot-posted reply contains any mapped word. A future colliding CI ChatOps mapping fails there instead of in production. A guard test asserts the ini parse is non-empty so neither can pass vacuously.

Handler complexity was pushed over the shrink-only ratchet by the new branch, so _actionable_change_key, _trigger_mode, and _refuse_retired_word were extracted along existing seams rather than raising the baseline.

Verification on the landed tree (abc3afd7db): AC1 43 passed; AC2/3/4 91 passed; AC5/5b/5c greps clean (retired word survives only in retrigger.py and test_review_bot_retrigger.py); make lint and make typecheck green. Note: the AC6 'tests/interfaces -k review_bot or retrigger' selection matches zero tests — there is no interfaces-layer coverage for this module; the meaningful AC6 evidence is lint + typecheck + the Verified +1 CI run.
